ES=F close · close 6,966.75

-3 extreme-down

ES=F closed 6966.75 on 20 November (from 7193.0, -3.15%) as the S&P 500 cash index fell 3.70% (-265.44) to 6,910.39, a seventh straight loss that put the index more than 10% below its 6 October record - correction territory - and capped an 8.61% week, its worst since April 2025 (CappNotes Closing Look, 20 November; AP closing data and UPI, 20 November). The Dow fell 1.93% (-949.73) to 48,147.33, also into correction. Breadth was 376 decliners to 123 advancers with 10 of 11 sectors lower - Technology -7.27%, Industrials -3.09%, Consumer Discretionary -2.95% against Consumer Staples +0.67% - while equal-weight RSP fell only 1.98%, 172bp better than the cap-weighted index, so the damage was concentrated in mega-cap tech. Nvidia fell 14.01% to $125.53, a 52-week low and roughly $491B of market value in one session, after Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues; Intuit -12.77%, Keysight -7.07%, BJ's -5.35% despite a beat and raise, against Gap +11.44% on an EPS beat. VIX +26.20% to 35.89, its highest close since April 2025, after touching about 40 intraday. Yields fell hard on haven demand: 2-year -13bp to 4.63%, 10-year -12bp to 4.92%, 30-year -9bp to 5.31%, 2s10s 29bp. High yield widened to 3.52% (19 November data) from 3.47%; HYG -0.26% while LQD +0.59%. Kalshi put a 25bp December hike at 90% and CME FedWatch at 98.4%. Final November UMich sentiment 51.5 (+7.3% m/m, in line) with one-year inflation expectations down to 3.7% from 4.3% at mid-month. WTI +0.93% to $83.98. RSI 25.12, with the close 9.1% below the 50-day (7663.91) and 5.6% below the 200-day (7377.81); 1H structure choppy, weekly structure uptrend.written Mon Nov 23, 9:42 AM ET · data through Fri Nov 20 close

That puts the 10-year roughly 24bp lower than the 5.14-5.16% it held on 17 November (news log) and 12bp below the 5.04% of 19 November. Final November UMich one-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.3% at mid-month. The ICE BofA MOVE index was 96.04 on 19 November, a normal-range reading below its 5 October high of 113.60 (StreetStats). -3 extreme-down

NQ=F closed 25291.0 on 20 November (from 26538.25, -4.70%) as the Nasdaq-100 cash index fell 5.61% (-1,488.07) to 25,028.98 and the Composite 5.28% (-1,261.47) to 22,617.73, taking the Composite below its 2025 close and erasing its 2026 gain; the Composite lost 10.02% on the week against the S&P 500's 8.61% (CappNotes Closing Look, 20 November; UPI and AP closing data, 20 November). Technology was the worst of the 11 S&P 500 sectors at -7.27%, with SMH -10.60%, the AI basket BAI -9.67%, computer storage devices -12.11% and semiconductors and related devices -10.43% (Market Digest, 20 November). Nvidia fell 14.01% to $125.53 - a 52-week low, roughly $491B of market value in a session and its worst day since DeepSeek - after Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues, with the SEC declining to comment; the WSJ had first reported an SEC investigation on 17 November without naming its focus. Anthropic fell 8.50% to $88.91, a second decline from its $97.17 debut close, with Sandisk -16.05%, Nebius -16.11%, Bloom Energy -15.30% and Intuit -12.77%. The sell-off was global: Nikkei -5.06% to 56,436.65 with SoftBank -14.48%, Kospi about -5.2%, TAIEX -6.23% for a record weekly loss, Stoxx 600 about -2%, Asia's worst week since 2020. Bitcoin -4.72% and ether -7.82%. VXN 45.25; QQQ saw a $1.29B outflow on 19 November data. RSI 27.04, with the close 14.0% below the 50-day (29395.23) and 10.3% below the 200-day (28201.69); 1H and weekly structure both choppy.written Mon Nov 23, 9:42 AM ET · data through Fri Nov 20 close

  • Market · High impact · Mon Nov 23, Pre-marketUS futures surge in a relief rally after seven straight S&P 500 losing sessions left the index and the Dow in correction territory. Nvidia leads an AI/chip bounce after Friday's 14% collapse; Trump posted over the weekend that Jensen Huang's return as CEO 'would be the best thing for the company,' while the FT reported Nvidia's board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about the job.
  • Policy · High impact · Mon Nov 23, Pre-marketAsian authorities moved to stabilize markets after last week's rout: Korea's finance ministry prepared a market stabilization fund of more than 10 trillion won (its first since 2008), Taiwan's regulator tightened short-selling rules, and Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing requirements. Kospi still fell sharply while Taiwan rallied; Europe opened higher.
  • Deals · High impact · Mon Nov 23, Pre-marketCrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, the largest cybersecurity takeover on record, pairing CrowdStrike's endpoint platform with Zscaler's network security and zero trust. Announced alongside CrowdStrike's Q3 FY2027 results, which showed a profit and a positive outlook.

  • Fed path · Nov 23 9:42amDecember-hike pricing firmed on 20 November: Kalshi put a 25bp hike at the 9 December FOMC at 90% (hold 9%, a larger hike 2%) against 89.3% the prior session, and CME FedWatch stood at 98.4% (CappNotes Closing Look, 19 and 20 November; news log, 20 November), after Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said rates must rise again on too-high inflation and Governors Cook and Waller reinforced December expectations (news log, 20 November; Market Digest, 20 November). The tightening is not US-only either: Barchart put a BoJ hike on 18 December at 79% and an ECB hike on 17 December at 91% (CappNotes Closing Look, 20 November), and Kitco's 20 November wrap frames the backdrop as 'an extended global central bank tightening cycle'. The 9 December FOMC falls outside all three horizons here (they mature 23 November, 30 November and 7 December), so this vote reflects accumulating pricing pressure, not the decision itself.

Bullish over a week.
  • Positioning and flows · Nov 23 9:42amTechnology positioning is the most de-grossed part of the market: Positioning is already washed out: Citadel Securities put aggregate CTA US-equity positioning at -3.3 standard deviations, sub-2nd percentile of its one-year range, as of 3 November, and Morgan Stanley's prime data had gross hedge-fund exposure down about 7.8% from peak as of 27 October - the largest de-grossing in its series back to 2016 - with US long/short gross leverage falling 8.7 points to 207.5% in the week to 6 November, the largest weekly drop since March 2020. These readings are 10-17 sessions before 20 November and reach this document only through secondary summaries, so they do not qualify for the crowd input, but as a direction they are a contrarian positive. The week to 6 November specifically saw hedge funds cutting technology exposure at a near-record pace. Bullish.
  • Earnings catalysts · Nov 23 9:42amThe Nvidia SEC accounting inquiry has no resolution date - Reuters could not determine when it began or which issues it covers, the SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond - leaving an open-ended overhang on the index's largest weight at a 52-week low of $125.53 (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, 20 November). An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing, but an unresolved one is a multi-day headwind. No earnings calendar for the 23-27 November week dated at or before 20 November was obtained, so only this overhang is voted. Bearish.
  • Macro calendar · Nov 23 9:42amThe 5-session window, maturing 30 November, contains the 25 November release of October PCE alongside the preliminary Q3 GDP revision, durable goods orders and jobless claims, with US markets closed 26 November for Thanksgiving and reduced liquidity expected (Kitco, 20 November; Market Digest, 20 November). Bearish for the longest-duration equity in the document.
